title: Build Signal: An Illustrated Tour of a Web Workflow
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A narrated, illustrated walkthrough of AI-assisted coding, GitHub review, hosting, and website checks.

cover.alt: Illustrated coding workbench connected to Git review and a hosted website with a health signal

content_html:
Build Signal presents a web development workflow as a guided page rather than a long list of tools. Its chapters move from AI-assisted coding through GitHub history and review to website hosting and a simple availability check.

The page combines three generated illustrations with browser speech. Visitors can choose a voice for each chapter, and the page remembers those choices in that browser. A closing conversation and a separate sign-off play as recorded audio with captions for the conversation.

The presentation is self-contained: one HTML page provides the layout and interactions, with no build step or third-party runtime script. The narration depends on voices installed in the visitor's browser or operating system, so the spoken experience can vary by device.

The tour distinguishes the pieces of the workflow. The repository's GitHub Actions check watches two URLs and emails a result; it does not deploy files. Hosting synchronization and its file-preservation settings are separate host configuration, not behavior supplied by this page.
